title: Live
summary: The live page puts your voice on air from this browser, sets the music level, and shows what is playing now.

entities.text: Your microphone, sent from this browser to the station. Only one session runs at a time. It keeps running while you open other pages; the mark in the header shows it.
How loud the microphone is. Speak so that it moves well into the bar; "Clipping" means you are too loud or too close.
The level of the music: normal, under voice, or off. While you are live, the music is lowered automatically by the ducking level in the settings.
The control link is the backend's connection to the playout engine; the output is the stream's connection to the stream server. Both must be connected for listeners to hear the station.

usage: Test the microphone first and watch the level. Go on air when ready, and stop when you are done. The music goes back to its normal level by itself.
steps: Choose the microphone and press "Test microphone".
Speak and check the level meter.
Press "Go on air" and wait for the state "On air".
mistakes: Opening the panel on a network address over plain HTTP. Browsers give the microphone only on localhost or HTTPS.
Playing a track preview through the speakers while live. The microphone may pick it up.
Closing or reloading the tab while live. It ends the voice; the browser asks first.

example.title: A short announcement
example.text: At 10:15 you want to announce a concert. Test the microphone, go on air, speak for a minute over the lowered music, and stop. The music comes back up within half a second.
